info.full_name: wastewater_covid
info.long_name: Wastewater Viral Activity Level of COVID-19
info.short_description: Wastewater Viral Activity Level of COVID-19.
info.long_description: Wastewater Viral Activity Level (VAL) of COVID-19. The viral activity level is the scaled number of standard deviations above a dynamic baseline. The baseline is the 10th percentile of the log-transformed and normalized concentration values, which is calculated within a 12 month timeframe every 6 months. This is then scaled, where e is the mathmatical constant, and x is the number of standard deviations: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">VAL = e^{x}</annotation></semantics></math> These values are categorized as very low, low, moderate, high, or very high using the following breakpoints: 1.5, 3, 4.5, and 8.
info.statement: The viral activity level of COVID-19 in wastewater is {value}.
info.unit: linear scaling of log standard deviations above a baseline

info.long_name: Number of COVID hospitalizations in the National Healthcare Safety Network
info.short_description: Weekly count of COVID-19 associated hospital admissions reported to CDC's NHSN.
info.long_description: The National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) is the nation's most widely used healthcare-associated infection tracking system. This dataset reports preliminary and finalized weekly hospital respiratory data and metrics aggregated to national and state/territory levels. Values are available for reference dates beginning August 2020. HHS collects data from state and territorial health departments about many, but not all, hospitals in the U.S. Notably excluded from this dataset are psychiatric and rehabilitation facilities, and religious non-medical facilities.

info.short_description: Estimated percentage of new hospital admissions with COVID-associated diagnoses, based on claims data from health system partners, smoothed in time using a Gaussian linear smoother
info.long_description: This data source is based on electronic medical records and claims data about hospital admissions, provided to Delphi by health system partners. We use this inpatient data to estimate the percentage of new hospital admissions with a COVID-associated diagnosis code in a given location, on a given day
info.unit: Percent of new hospital admissions, smoothed

sources.location: COVIDcast > Hospital Admissions

info.long_description: This data source is based on information about outpatient visits, provided to CMU/Delphi by health system partners. Using this outpatient data, CMU/Delphi estimates the percentage of COVID-related doctor's visits in a given location, on a given day. Percent of all unique outpatient visits with primary ICD-10 code of any of: U071, U072, B9729, J1281, Z03818, B342, J1289

info.long_name: Wastewater Viral Activity Level of Influenza A
info.short_description: Wastewater Viral Activity Level of Influenza A.
info.long_description: Wastewater Viral Activity Level (VAL) of Influenza A. The viral activity level is the scaled number of standard deviations above a dynamic baseline. The baseline is the 10th percentile of the log-transformed and normalized concentration values, which is calculated within a 18 month timeframe every year. This is then scaled, where e is the mathmatical constant, and x is the number of standard deviations: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">VAL = e^{x}</annotation></semantics></math> These values are categorized as very low, low, moderate, high, or very high using the following breakpoints: 1.6, 4.5, 12.2, and 20.1.
info.statement: The viral activity level of Influenza A in wastewater is {value}.
info.unit: linear scaling of log standard deviations above a baseline

info.long_name: Number of influenza hospitalizations in the National Healthcare Safety Network
info.short_description: Weekly count of influenza-associated hospital admissions reported to CDC's NHSN.
info.long_description: The National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) is the nation's most widely used healthcare-associated infection tracking system. This dataset reports preliminary and finalized weekly hospital respiratory data and metrics aggregated to national and state/territory levels. Values are available for reference dates beginning August 2020. HHS collects data from state and territorial health departments about many, but not all, hospitals in the U.S. Notably excluded from this dataset are psychiatric and rehabilitation facilities, and religious non-medical facilities.

info.long_name: Percentage of Hospital Admissions with Influenza Diagnosis
info.short_description: Estimated percentage of new hospital admissions with influenza-associated diagnoses, based on claims data from health system partners, smoothed in time using a Gaussian linear smoother
info.long_description: This data source is based on electronic medical records and claims data about hospital admissions, provided to Delphi by health system partners. We use this inpatient data to estimate the percentage of new hospital admissions with an influenza-associated diagnosis code in a given location, on a given day
info.unit: Percent of new hospital admissions, smoothed

info.long_name: Weighted Percent of Visits for Influenza-Like Illness from ILINet
info.short_description: Population-weighted percentage of outpatient visits for influenza-like illness.
info.long_description: Weighted percent of visits for influenza-like illness (ILI) reported by outpatient healthcare providers through the CDC ILINet surveillance network. ILI is defined as fever (temperature of 100F or greater) and a cough and/or sore throat without a known cause other than influenza. The weighted percentage adjusts for differences in state population sizes to provide a more representative national and regional estimate. Data are available from 1997 week 40 onward and are typically published weekly on Fridays. This data is mirrored from the CDC FluView surveillance system via the CMU Delphi Epidata API.

info.short_description: Share of Kinsa smart thermometer users reporting cough, cold, or flu symptoms.
info.long_description: The Kinsa Cough, Cold & Flu signal is derived from anonymized illness data collected via Kinsa smart thermometers and the associated mobile app. The signal represents the share of active users who reported symptoms consistent with cough, cold, or flu on a given day at the national level. Data are available daily starting in 2018.

info.short_description: Wastewater Viral Activity Level of RSV.
info.long_description: Wastewater Viral Activity Level (VAL) of RSV. The viral activity level is the scaled number of standard deviations above a dynamic baseline. The baseline is the 10th percentile of the log-transformed and normalized concentration values, which is calculated within a 18 month timeframe every year. This is then scaled, where e is the mathmatical constant, and x is the number of standard deviations: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">VAL = e^{x}</annotation></semantics></math> These values are categorized as very low, low, moderate, high, or very high using the following breakpoints: 4, 8, 12, and 20.
info.statement: The viral activity level of RSV in wastewater is {value}.
info.unit: linear scaling of log standard deviations above a baseline

info.long_name: Weighted Percent of Visits for Influenza-Like Illness from ILINet
info.short_description: Population-weighted percentage of outpatient visits for influenza-like illness.
info.long_description: Weighted percent of visits for influenza-like illness (ILI) reported by outpatient healthcare providers through the CDC ILINet surveillance network. ILI is defined as fever (temperature of 100F or greater) and a cough and/or sore throat without a known cause other than influenza. The weighted percentage adjusts for differences in state population sizes to provide a more representative national and regional estimate. Data are available from 1997 week 40 onward and are typically published weekly on Fridays. This data is mirrored from the CDC FluView surveillance system via the CMU Delphi Epidata API.
